facts: The Project Gutenberg eBook of "The Great Gatsby" was released on January 17, 2021.
The eBook was last updated on January 26, 2025.
The eBook was produced by Alex Cabal for the Standard Ebooks project.
The text includes a dedication to Zelda.
The narrator's family is prominent in a Midwestern city.
He moved to the East after World War I to pursue a career in the bond business.
Daisy expresses a desire for her daughter to be a "beautiful little fool."
Nick observes Gatsby standing alone, reaching toward a distant green light.
The area known as the "valley of ashes" is described as desolate.
Tom Buchanan introduces Myrtle Wilson to the narrator at her husband's garage.
Tom violently strikes Myrtle when she mentions his wife, Daisy.
The trio travels to New York to host a gathering in a cramped apartment.
Jay Gatsby hosts extravagant summer parties at his mansion.
The narrator feels out of place despite having a formal invitation.
A guest's car crashes during one of the parties.
The narrator works at the Probity Trust during the summer.
Gatsby's mansion hosts extravagant summer parties attended by notable figures from East and West Egg.

Mr. Wolfshiem, a gambler linked to the 1919 World Series scandal, praises Gatsby during a lunch.
Daisy marries Tom Buchanan after a tumultuous moment involving a distressing letter.

Gatsby's collection of beautiful shirts brings Daisy to tears during their reunion.
Gatsby realizes that the green light across the bay has lost its significance now that Daisy is with him.
Gatsby was originally named James Gatz.
Dan Cody was Gatsby's mentor who introduced him to wealth.
Gatsby hosts lavish parties to attract Daisy Buchanan.
Daisy Buchanan arrives at one of Gatsby's parties with her husband, Tom.
Gatsby dismisses his servants, prompting speculation about his health.
Daisy admits her past feelings for Tom during a confrontation in town.
Myrtle dies in a hit-and-run involving Gatsby's car, which Daisy was driving.
Tom feigns concern over Myrtle's death while distancing himself from the incident.
The narrator struggles to sleep due to a foghorn and unsettling dreams.
Gatsby waits for Daisy, who never arrives.
George Wilson seeks revenge at Gatsby's home after the loss of his wife Myrtle.
Gatsby's death results from a tragic confrontation.
Gatsby's funeral was attended only by Mr. Gatz, Nick, and a few others.
Mr. Gatz arrived from Minnesota after Gatsby's death.
Nick Carraway struggles with isolation while trying to reach out to Daisy and Gatsby's acquaintances.
Tom Buchanan represents the carelessness of the wealthy elite in the narrative.
